---
description: "How NCodeGroup code emits logs, audit events, metrics and traces: keeping secrets and unbounded values out of telemetry, making sure each fact is recorded exactly once by the component that owns it, and following the family's conventions for log messages, event IDs, meters, activity sources and log sinks."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.csproj, **/Program.cs, **/Dockerfile, **/*.Dockerfile, **/appsettings*.json, **/launchSettings.json"
---

# Logging and telemetry

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Never write access, refresh or ID tokens, session handles, cookie values, OAuth state, authorization codes, keys or other secrets to logs, audit records, exception messages, span tags or metric attributes. Never return them from an endpoint, and never keep them beyond the request, for example in HttpContext.Items.** These values grant access. Once one is in telemetry, anyone who can read the logs or traces can use the credential. *Check:* Look for log arguments, audit details, Activity tags, metric tags, exception messages, response bodies or HttpContext.Items entries that carry a token, handle, cookie, state, code, key or secret value. *Note:* The backend-for-frontend doc also bans user subjects and request paths from every signal. Other sources allow identifiers such as subject on traces, logs and audit records (never on metrics), and audit records carry a verified subject_id. Follow the stricter rule in browser-session/BFF code. <sub>Identity ADR-0290; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Never use a tenant, client, subject or user identifier, a network address or host, a request path, or any other unbounded or free-form value as a metric attribute. Put those values on traces and logs instead. Per-entity usage that must be reported belongs in a durable store that an API reads.** Every distinct attribute value creates a new time series. Unbounded dimensions grow with the customer base until the metrics backend drops data, and they also leak identifying data. *Check:* Look for Counter.Add, Histogram.Record, TagList or KeyValuePair tags whose values come from tenant, client, subject or user ids, IP addresses, hosts, URLs or paths, user agents, trace ids, or free-form names such as an environment name. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity ADR-0199; Identity ADR-0283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Take every metric or telemetry dimension value from a vocabulary the server controls (registered names, server-chosen codes or constants), never directly from request input or free-form user text. Map any value outside the registered set to `_OTHER`. Do not branch behavior on free-form display names either.** If request input can set a dimension value, any caller can create series at will and exhaust the backend's series limit. Arbitrary text also has no fixed meaning. *Check:* Look for tags or dimensions set straight from grant_type, method, headers, URIs or display names without first checking them against a registered set and falling back to `_OTHER`. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0289</sub>
- **Record an audit event, log or notification for a state change only when the operation's own result shows that this call made the change, for example a non-zero affected count or a won claim. Concurrent paths that end or revoke the same entity must go through one shared claiming path.** When another request already made the change, auditing anyway records the same change twice, and concurrent paths can terminate, log and notify for one entity more than once. *Check:* Look for audit, event or log emission after reading an entity that is not gated on the write's returned count or success, and for handlers that bypass the shared claim and dispatch termination directly. <sub>Identity ADR-0215; Identity ADR-0227</sub>
- **Publish protocol-error audit events from one central filter that wraps the endpoint group, never from the individual sites that create or throw an error. Any new result type that carries an error must expose that error to the filter.** Only a central funnel covers every error exactly once. Publishing at each site leaves a silent gap at the first forgotten site, and an error that is both created and thrown gets published twice. A result type that hides its error from the filter leaves the error unaudited. *Check:* Look for error-audit publishes next to code that builds, returns or throws a protocol error instead of in the filter, and for new error-carrying result types the filter cannot inspect. <sub>Identity ADR-0049</sub>
- **Publish audit events for state-changing successes (create, update, delete, revoke, block) at their call site, including every management API change to a security-relevant resource. When an administrator performs the action, attribute the event to that administrator, in addition to any per-entity audit.** Successful responses never pass through an error funnel, so the call site is the only place that can record them, and administrative actions must be traceable to whoever performed them. *Check:* Look for new state-changing endpoints or success paths with no audit publish, ones that expect the error filter to record them, and admin actions whose audit does not identify the acting administrator. <sub>Identity ADR-0049; Identity ADR-0226; Identity ADR-0100; Identity ADR-0098</sub>
- **Give every failure path, security rejection and lifecycle transition the same observability that equivalent paths already have. Use a distinct audit event or reason for each distinct cause, for example an untrusted certificate versus a subject mismatch, or a retry versus a rotation versus a replay. Record nothing for a request that was simply refused, and send the paths for one outcome through one shared method.** An unobserved failure path leaves the capability only partly delivered, and a shared reason stops operators from telling a trust failure, a client retry or an attack apart. *Check:* Look for catch blocks, rejection branches (anti-forgery, Fetch Metadata, authorization denial) or session create/expire/terminate paths that emit no log or audit event while similar paths do, and for distinct causes reported under the same event or reason. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review; Identity ADR-0173; Identity ADR-0217; Identity ADR-0292; Identity ADR-0229; Identity ADR-0098</sub>
- **When an error audit must happen once per request, enforce it with a constant sentinel key in HttpContext.Items, not with the error object's reference or hash code. On a thrown-error path, publish the audit before rendering the response.** The invariant is one audit per errored request. A key based on the error object weakens that to one per object, and a hash key can suppress a different error. Publishing first means the record exists even when rendering throws. *Check:* Look for dedup keyed on an error instance or a non-constant Items key, and for exception handlers that publish the audit only after, or only when, the response renders successfully. <sub>Identity ADR-0049</sub>
- **Run the rate-limit check before the exception and audit filters, so that a refused (429) request raises no audit event and no domain event. Instrument such flood-path mechanisms directly instead of through the event pipeline.** An attacker who floods an endpoint should not also flood the audit log, and pushing refusals through the event pipeline would bring back the load the limiter exists to shed. *Check:* Check the filter order, and look for 429 paths that publish audit or domain events. <sub>Identity ADR-0196; Identity ADR-0197</sub>
- **Do not log, audit or count a fact at the call site when an event is published for that same fact. Logging, metrics and tracing for domain outcomes come from handlers that subscribe to the event stream. Keep inline logger calls for mechanics such as cache misses, retries and diagnostics.** The event stream is the single source for logs, audit records, metrics and traces. A parallel log or counter duplicates the fact, scatters templates and EventIds, and drifts from the event count. *Check:* Look for logger calls or Counter.Add calls beside a PublishAsync/Record*Async for the same outcome, and for failure paths that catch and log where they should publish a failure audit event. <sub>Identity ADR-0047; Identity ADR-0197</sub>
- **Do not write audit or telemetry records to a database inline on the request path. Enqueue them on a bounded in-memory queue that a hosted background service flushes in batches. When the queue is full and drops items, count the drops and log the count once per flush interval.** An inline write adds a database round trip to every audited operation and lets a failed audit fail the operation. Logging each drop floods the log exactly when the system is overloaded. *Check:* Look for event or audit handlers that call a store, DbContext or SaveChanges during the request, and for full-queue paths that drop items silently or log once per item. <sub>Identity ADR-0303</sub>
- **A final flush at shutdown must never throw. Log any data it cannot persist as a discarded-data warning with a dedicated event ID, and when the stop token ends the wait, log the held data as discarded and return. Do not log a cancelled periodic flush as a failure: leave its batch for the next flush.** An exception during shutdown breaks host disposal, and the log is the only record of lost data. Cancellation is not an error, so a warning for it is noise. *Check:* Look for shutdown flushes that can let exceptions escape or drop data without a warning, and for catch blocks that log OperationCanceledException from a cancelled flush as a warning or error. <sub>Identity ADR-0209</sub>
- **Log a dependency outage once per state change: one warning with the exception when the breaker opens and one information message when it closes, never once per failing request.** An outage should produce one log line per replica, not one per request. *Check:* Look for warnings or errors logged inside the per-request failure path of a fail-open dependency call. <sub>Identity ADR-0196</sub>
- **Rate-limit rejection logs use a stable event ID and only bounded fields: tenant, partition name, limit and window. They never include the remote address, the client ID or the raw partition value.** The log must identify which limit was hit without recording caller identifiers. *Check:* Look for rate-limit or quota log calls that have no EventId, or whose parameters include an IP address, client_id or partition key value. <sub>Identity ADR-0196; Identity ADR-0246</sub>
- **In audit records, put the failure as a required machine-readable error code (for example an OAuth error code), with any prose in a separate message field. Fill the subject id only with a verified subject. On a failed authentication, record a caller-supplied user name in a separate details member such as `attempted_username`.** Investigators group failures by a code field, and subject_id is only trustworthy if it never holds unauthenticated input. *Check:* Look for failure events with no code or with prose only, and for failure paths that set SubjectId from a user name, login hint or other unauthenticated input. <sub>Identity ADR-0283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Log audit entries at the level mapped from the event's severity (info → Information, warning → Warning, critical → Critical), not at one fixed level.** A category filter set to Warning can then keep failures and critical events and drop routine successes. *Check:* Look for audit logging calls with a hard-coded LogLevel. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Choose levels for handled conditions on purpose. Log an expected, client-recoverable condition (such as a concurrency conflict turned into 412) at Debug. Log a known failure mapped to an error response once, at Warning. Log a skipped unreadable stored document at Warning with its owning identifiers and the exception Message. Each of these gets its own event ID.** Expected conditions must not raise alarms, and operators need the same identifiers in the log that the caller or the diagnostic report received. *Check:* Look for handled, expected conditions logged at Warning or Error, known failures mapped to responses with no log, a missing or reused event ID, or a log that leaves out the identifying fields. <sub>Identity ADR-0214; Identity ADR-0245; Identity ADR-0241</sub>
- **When a change that cannot be refused (configuration reload, deployment) makes stored entities invalid, log a warning that names each affected entity and its violations, and keep starting up.** Refusing to start would let one entity take down every replica and tenant, and without a report the broken entities would go unnoticed. *Check:* Look for configuration-change paths that silently leave stored entities invalid, or that throw at startup because of one invalid entity. <sub>Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **Log through source-generated `[LoggerMessage]` extension methods kept in a per-package `internal static partial class Log` marked `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`. A direct `ILogger.Log*` call is allowed only as an approved exception, and needs a `//` comment at the call that cites the decision permitting it.** Generated logging is allocation-free, strongly typed and structured. The generator does not check the keys of a direct call, so each exception has to be visible and justified. *Check:* Look for direct logger.LogInformation/LogWarning/Log calls without a comment citing the decision, and for a Log class missing [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-0283</sub>
- **Make log message templates constants with named placeholders, never interpolated or concatenated strings, and pass each value as its own typed argument instead of a pre-built ToString().** This keeps logs structured, and formatting happens only when the level is enabled. *Check:* Look for `$"..."` or `+` in templates, and for `.ToString()` on log arguments. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Treat log event IDs as append-only. Define them as named constants in a per-package `internal static class EventIds` (a private `Base` plus an offset, each named like its `[LoggerMessage]` method), keep each runtime package inside its own disjoint 1000-wide band, and never renumber a shipped ID or reuse a retired or reserved one. Abstractions packages log nothing.** Stable, globally unique IDs keep log queries and alerts reliable. A reused ID would make existing filters match an unrelated event. *Check:* Look for `EventId = 1234` literals, constants whose names don't match their method, changed or reused IDs, IDs outside the package's band, or logging added to an Abstractions package. <sub>Identity ADR-0167; Identity ADR-0246; Identity ADR-0283; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Log a structured record as flattened key/value attributes, with numbers kept as numbers, not as one serialized JSON string. Flatten only one level, write arrays and nested values as raw JSON text, and leave out null members.** A collector cannot index fields inside an opaque string, and flattening only one level keeps the number of index fields an event can create bounded. *Check:* Look for JsonSerializer.Serialize output passed as a single log property, flattening that expands arrays element by element or recurses without limit, and null-valued keys being emitted. <sub>Identity ADR-0283; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Declare telemetry names once, as public constants: the meter name, the activity source name, and the field and attribute names. Use the same name for one concept in the audit record, the log state, the span tags and the metric attributes, with only a namespace prefix changing.** Hosts and dashboards subscribe and filter by these names, and operators can move from a log entry to its trace and metrics only when the names match. *Check:* Look for inline string literals for meter, source, tag or field names, and for one concept named differently across signals. <sub>Identity ADR-0283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Measure each signal once, through its owner. Request counts, latency and status come from ASP.NET Core's `http.server.request.duration`, enriched through `IHttpMetricsTagsFeature`, and outbound calls come from System.Net.Http. Do not create spans for inbound requests or bare HttpClient calls. Add your own instruments or spans only for mechanisms these do not cover, such as waits and store operations.** A duplicate instrument or span doubles the series a deployment pays for, drifts from the built-in one, and gives conflicting data. *Check:* Look for new Counter or Histogram instruments that count or time HTTP requests or HttpClient calls, and StartActivity calls that only wrap an endpoint handler or a single HttpClient call. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity ADR-0270; Identity ADR-0298; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When a host collects `System.Net.Http` metrics and outbound calls can go to user- or client-registered URIs, configure a view that drops `server.address` and `server.port`.** The hosts of client-registered URIs are unbounded and identifying, so these attributes create unbounded series. *Check:* Look for AddMeter("System.Net.Http") without a view that filters out server.address and server.port. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **Library packages instrument only through `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` and `ActivitySource`. They take no OpenTelemetry API or SDK dependency, configure no exporters or listeners, and their registration helpers never turn on tracing. The host wires up OpenTelemetry (not vendor-specific SDKs) and opts in to each package's sources.** An SDK dependency in a library is forced on every consumer, and instruments cost nothing until a listener subscribes. Open standards let the host swap vendors. *Check:* Look for OpenTelemetry package references or usings in library projects, MeterListener or exporter setup in library code, metrics extension methods that call AddSource or build a tracer provider, and vendor APM SDK dependencies anywhere. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity ADR-0298; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity ADR-0134</sub>
- **Create meters through `IMeterFactory`, never `new Meter(...)`. Each package has one meter, named after the package by a public constant. Its instruments are defined once in one internal singleton metrics class, and call sites call methods on that class instead of the instrument APIs.** The factory scopes meters to their service provider, so hosts in one process don't share instruments and tests can read them with MetricCollector<T>. Defining instruments in one place keeps each one defined once. *Check:* Look for `new Meter(` in library code, a meter name written as a literal, several meters in one package, or CreateCounter/CreateHistogram/Add/Record calls outside the metrics class. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>
- **A package that traces uses one static ActivitySource whose name equals the package's meter name, exposed as a public constant. On failure a span sets ActivityStatusCode.Error and `error.type`. Each span mirrors one duration histogram: it is named like the histogram without `.duration` and carries the same bounded attributes.** Matching names let a host subscribe to a package's metrics and traces with one wildcard. ActivitySource has no factory, so it cannot be scoped per provider, and one vocabulary then describes both signals. *Check:* Look for several ActivitySources in one package, source names that differ from the meter name, spans without a matching histogram or with different tags, and failure paths that don't set Error status and error.type. <sub>Identity ADR-0298; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Prefix instrument and attribute names with the family namespace (`ncode.{product}.{area}...`), but use the OpenTelemetry semantic-convention name wherever one exists (such as `error.type`, `http.route`, `http.response.status_code`).** A host can then subscribe to the whole family with one wildcard, and the standard attributes stay interoperable. *Check:* Look for new instrument or attribute names without the family prefix, and for custom renames of attributes that the semantic conventions define. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use UCUM units. Record durations as histograms in seconds (`s`) with explicit bucket advice, and give counters a curly-brace annotation unit such as `{request}` or `{event}`.** Consistent units let dashboards and alerts compare instruments without conversion. *Check:* Look for durations in milliseconds or with no unit or bucket advice, and for counters with no unit or a unit that isn't an annotation. <sub>Identity ADR-0197; Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Set `error.type` only when the operation fails, using a bounded failure-reason constant or the exception's full type name. For protocol errors, set the error-code attribute in the one shared writer that every error response path goes through.** Exception messages are unbounded, and HTTP status alone cannot tell error codes apart. Tagging in one place keeps every path consistent. *Check:* Look for error.type set on success paths or from ex.Message/ex.ToString(), and for error response paths that write a protocol error without the error-code attribute or tag it outside the shared writer. <sub>Identity docs/metrics.md; Identity ADR-0197</sub>
- **Route every call from a shared-state or cache adapter through one measuring wrapper that records the duration, records `error.type` on an exception, and rethrows.** Repeating timing and error recording in each adapter method lets the metrics drift apart. *Check:* Look for adapter methods with their own Stopwatch and try/catch metric code, and for new adapter methods that skip the wrapper. <sub>Identity ADR-0246</sub>
- **Library code never registers, removes or configures logging providers or console formatters (no AddConsole, AddJsonConsole, AddSimpleConsole, AddEventLog, ClearProviders or FormatterName). Only the host's composition root chooses the sinks.** Sinks and output format belong to the host, and a library that picks them takes that decision away. *Check:* Look for ILoggingBuilder provider or formatter calls inside package extension methods rather than a host's Program.cs. <sub>Identity ADR-0210; Identity ADR-0248; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **In a host's composition root, call `builder.Logging.ClearProviders()` and then add the console provider (writing to stdout) and the EventSource provider explicitly. Never write application-managed log files. Every process that runs from the same image, such as a migration worker, sets up console logging the same way and binds the same `Logging:Console` configuration.** The default providers differ by platform: the Windows Event Log provider fills the Application log and throws when written to after disposal. File logs break read-only, stateless containers, and every process should emit the format the collector expects. *Check:* Look for a host Program.cs that keeps the default providers or adds EventLog, Debug or file sinks, and for worker entry points that hard-code a formatter or skip configuration binding. <sub>Identity ADR-0210; Identity ADR-0134; Identity ADR-0248</sub>
- **The production stage of a host container image sets `Logging__Console__FormatterName=json`, `Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__UseUtcTimestamp=true` and `Logging__Console__FormatterOptions__TimestampFormat=O`. Debug stages, launchSettings and appsettings used by local runs keep the `simple` formatter.** Collectors read stdout one line at a time, so the multi-line simple format splits entries and separates exceptions from them, and UTC timestamps sort across replicas. A person reads local and debug consoles, and JSON is harder to read by eye. *Check:* Look for a Dockerfile final stage that is missing any of the three variables or uses other values, and for the JSON formatter forced in base or debug stages, launchSettings or local appsettings. <sub>Identity ADR-0248</sub>
